title: NYC weekly 311 service requests
brief: Revision 2 applies the owner's decisions (2026-11-08). Entrants forecast how many NYC 311 service requests (all complaint types, citywide) will be created in a Monday-to-Sunday New York week. Forecasts lock Sunday 23:59 ET; the first scored lock is Sun 2026-12-13, together with Seattle. Rounds resolve on the archived snapshot of Tuesday 12:00 ET eight days after the week ends. Zero point: mean_k with k=4 and an rms13 spread, i.e. the mean of the four weeks complete at lock, with sd equal to the root-mean-square of its own errors over the 13 most recent complete weeks. It is one setting of a single parameterised reference family. Population: all requests. Route: the automated daily SODA fetch, with a manual weekly download as the documented fallback. Reviewer decision for maintainers: the rights verdict (approved is proposed, not granted). It waits on one person task written out in Source: reading the NYC.gov Terms of Use in a browser, because that page returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches.
question: How many NYC 311 service requests (rows of NYC Open Data dataset erm2-nwe9, all complaint types, agencies and statuses) will have a created_date in the target week, Monday 00:00 to the next Monday 00:00, New York local time?

source.publisher: NYC 311 and the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI), published on NYC Open Data (data.cityofnewyork.us). Dataset metadata: attribution '311', provenance 'official', custom fields 'Automation: Yes', 'Update Frequency: Daily', agency OTI [verified, api/views/erm2-nwe9.json fetched 2026-11-09T00:58:23Z].
source.access: Primary route (automated): the Socrata SODA endpoint https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/erm2-nwe9.json. No key, no app token and no account. Ten aggregate queries on 2026-11-09 00:58Z-01:12Z all returned HTTP 200 [verified]. One request a day, archived: GET https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/erm2-nwe9.json?$select=date_trunc_ymd(created_date) as d, agency, count(*) as n&$where=created_date >= '<fetch day - 280 days>T00:00:00'&$group=d, agency&$order=d, agency&$limit=50000. That is about 4,500 rows, about 260 KB a day [inferred: 10,801 rows and 628,157 bytes for the 798-day capture of 2026-11-09, scaled to 280 days]. Why 280 days: the spread rule searches up to 26 weeks of past target weeks (back to D-189). Each of those weeks needs its own four reference weeks (back to D-224) and a 28-day outage lookback (back to D-252), plus margin. Why agency is in the grouping: it lets the outage check see when one agency's feed drops out (missing_data_policy). count(*) equals count(distinct unique_key): both gave 80,626 for the week of 2026-10-26 [verified]. The cheaper count(*) is used. The response headers must be recorded with the body: X-SODA2-Data-Out-Of-Date, X-SODA2-Truth-Last-Modified and Last-Modified. A body served with X-SODA2-Data-Out-Of-Date: true is refused, never archived as a capture. This matters: 3 of the agent's 10 queries were answered by a stale secondary. It was flagged Out-Of-Date: true, its truth time was 2026-11-05 02:46:28Z (three days old) and it took 59-68 s. Fresh answers (truth 2026-11-08 02:40:03Z) took 23-32 s [verified]. The doc's '~80 s' queries are probably this secondary [inferred]. One stale answer also ended in a connection reset after the body (curl 56). Timeout 180 s. The doc's sample code uses 60 s, which a stale-secondary answer would exceed. A refused or failed fetch is not retried in a loop (lesson 5). The next scheduled refresh tries again. Archive: the body is saved exactly as served to sources/nyc311/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json, with url, fetched_at, sha256, bytes and the three headers in sources/manifest.json through ssa/provenance.py (docs/sources.md §4). Do not register an app token. The refresh runs on datacenter runners and that route is untested from here. The data endpoint answered this sandbox, but the city's policy pages returned Akamai 403. A 403 or 429 on the data endpoint from the runners means a local courier (lesson 3). Fallback route (manual, used only if maintainers rule that automated retrieval is not allowed): see archive_policy.
source.archive_policy: Use: allowed [verified, city law]. Automated retrieval: allowed by intent [inferred]. Redistribution of the archived aggregate bodies: allowed [inferred]. Evidence: (a) NYC Administrative Code §23-502(d): public data sets 'shall be made available without any registration requirement, license requirement or restrictions on their use', provided the department may require a third party to 'explicitly identify the source and version of the public data set, and a description of any modifications'. The same clause adds that 'restrictions' excludes 'measures required to ensure access to public data sets, to protect the single web site ... from unlawful abuse'. §23-502(b): data sets 'shall be in a format that permits automated processing'. §23-503(a): 'The department may take reasonable measures to maintain bandwidth availability of the web portal.' [verified text, read on the nyc-laws.readthedocs.io mirror fetched 2026-11-09T01:11:12Z; whether that mirror is current against the official American Legal code is unverified]. (b) Dataset metadata says 'Automation: Yes'. It has no licenseId field [verified 00:58Z]. (c) The portal FAQ reads 'There are no restrictions on the use of Open Data. Refer to Terms of Use for more information.' [unverified here: seen only in a search-engine snippet; opendata.cityofnewyork.us/faq/ returned an Akamai 'Access Denied' 403 to an honest user agent at 2026-11-09T01:10:35Z]. (d) The portal Terms of Use (www.nyc.gov/html/data/terms.html) returned 403 at 01:11:15Z. A search snippet says use binds the user to 'all of the Terms of Use of NYC.gov as well as the Privacy Policy' and to 'any additional terms of use defined by entities providing data or feeds'. Whether the NYC.gov terms contain a clause on automated access, like the Open NY bullet found for MTA (lesson 10), is unverified. That text is the one gap. A person must read it in a browser; the agent did not route around the 403. Condition to meet: cite 'NYC 311 / NYC Open Data, 311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present (erm2-nwe9)' with the snapshot date, and say the archive is unmodified. Route (owner decision, rev 2): A, the automated daily fetch, once a person has read the NYC.gov Terms in a browser. The manual weekly download below is the documented fallback. Proposed arena inventory row: rights 'approved', proposed for the maintainers to decide. The agent does not grant it. PERSON TASK (owner rule G4), done by an SSA maintainer before the adapter merges to main. Open in an ordinary browser https://www.nyc.gov/html/data/terms.html, the NYC.gov Terms of Use it links to, and https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/faq/. Save each page as PDF into the PR, with the date. Answer three questions, quoting each clause and its section heading (lesson 10). (i) Does any clause restrict access by automated means (script, bot, crawler, scraper, API polling, rate)? (ii) Does any clause restrict keeping copies or republishing data or derived counts? (iii) Does any dataset-specific term apply to erm2-nwe9? If (i) bars or is unclear about API retrieval, use the manual fallback, and the maintainer sends the message below. If (ii) bars archiving, the source stops, the card returns to draft, and the maintainer sends the message below. MESSAGE (exact text, sent only by the maintainer, to the contact address the Open Data portal lists for questions; nobody on our side sends anything before that). Subject: Automated access and archiving of 311 Service Requests (erm2-nwe9). Body: 'Hello, we run the Social Simulation Arena, a public, non-commercial research benchmark. We would like to read daily aggregate counts from the dataset 311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present (erm2-nwe9) through one SODA API query a day, without an app token, and archive each response unchanged so that published scores can be reproduced. We would cite NYC 311 / NYC Open Data and the snapshot date. Is this consistent with the NYC Open Data and NYC.gov Terms of Use? Is there a request rate or time of day you would prefer? Thank you.' Manual-download fallback (YouGov-crosstab pattern, tools/ingest_yougov_xtab.py on origin/dev), if that reading bars automated retrieval but a person may download and SSA may keep a copy: WHO: one person named by the maintainers, with a named backup. WHEN: once a week, Sunday 08:00-20:00 ET, after Saturday evening's load (about 21:40 ET) and before the lock. The data does not change between Saturday's and Sunday's loads for any week the file is used for. WHAT: the person opens the exact SODA URL above (fetch day = that Sunday) in a browser and saves the JSON. The bytes are the same as the automated request's, so the parser is shared. INGEST: a new tools/ingest_nyc311.py, modelled on ingest_yougov_xtab.py, checks that the JSON parses into (day, agency, count) rows. It checks freshness: the newest day with a full count must be Friday (capture day - 2) and must pass the outage check, which proves the body did not come from a stale secondary. It checks that the four reference weeks, their outage lookback and the target week being resolved are all present and pass the outage checks. It also refuses a capture day earlier than the newest archive, and an existing same-day archive with different bytes. It writes sources/nyc311/<capture-day>.json with its sha256. USE: one Sunday file serves the lock reference for that night's round and resolves the round whose week ended six days earlier (Sunday W+13). Manual mode therefore resolves at +6 days instead of +8. Measured missing fraction at that capture: median 0.004%, max 0.76% (41 weeks), against 0.003% and 0.73% at the Tuesday snapshot. A round states its mode when posted and never switches. MISSED DOWNLOAD: no Sunday capture by 20:00 ET means that night's round is not posted, which is announced before the lock. The round due to resolve may use a late capture until Wednesday 12:00 ET, which then serves resolution only. After that it is cancelled. Two missed Sundays in a row pause the family until maintainers review.

target.population: All rows of erm2-nwe9: every complaint type, responding agency, status and submission channel, as the owner's doc specifies (owner decision, rev 2: population A). Citywide, with no geographic split in the regular tier. The dataset describes itself as 'only service requests that can be directed to specific agencies'. General 311 information calls are not in it [verified, dataset description].
target.window: Monday 00:00 inclusive to the following Monday 00:00 exclusive, New York local time, on created_date. created_date is a Socrata floating timestamp, taken as New York local time, as in the doc [inferred, not checked against an hourly profile]. Weeks with a DST change have 167 or 169 hours and are counted as published.
target.calculation: Sum over the seven target days and all agencies of n from the resolution snapshot, where n = count(*) per (date_trunc_ymd(created_date), agency). Rows equal distinct unique_key values (80,626 = 80,626 for the week of 2026-10-26) [verified for one week; re-check in implementation].

lock: Sunday 23:59 America/New_York immediately before the target week, stored in UTC (04:59Z on the Monday in EST, 03:59Z in EDT). This is the doc's rule and the arena's rule for behavioural series. There is no publisher release calendar, so the round text says that SSA both sets and resolves this metric (docs/sources.md §1.1), and the definition is committed with a timestamp before the first window opens. The lock reference is read from the last fresh capture (Out-Of-Date false) taken in the 24 h before the lock. If there is none, the round is not posted (lesson 13). Posting: the data loads once a day at about 02:40Z, which is 21:40 EST. Each load carries rows created up to about 02:00 of the load day, so Saturday is complete and Sunday is absent at the lock [verified from two loads: truth 2026-11-05 02:46Z had newest created_date 2026-11-04T02:05; truth 2026-11-08 02:40Z had 557 rows for 2026-11-07]. Whether the load time is fixed in UTC or in ET across DST is unverified. First scored lock (owner decision, rev 2): Sun 2026-12-13 23:59 ET, for the week Mon 2026-12-14 to Sun 2026-12-20, resolution Tue 2026-12-29 12:00 ET. It ships in the same main merge as the Seattle calls family, whose first scored lock is the same night. Working back from it: the fill-in confirmation check (see Resolution) needs daily captures from Tue 2026-12-08. The adapter and the round must therefore be on main, with the scheduled refresh running, by Sun 2026-11-29, which leaves participants 14 days (lesson 7). The earliest possible date, Sun 2026-12-06 (needing main by 11-22), was not chosen. The next round, the Christmas week of 2026-12-21, is flagged in its question text.
baseline: Ranked zero point (owner decision, rev 2): mean_k with k=4 and an rms13 spread, written 'mean4' below. It is the mean of the four most recent Monday-to-Sunday weeks settled at lock, starting D-35, D-28, D-21 and D-14, where D is the target Monday. The week D-7 to D-1 is never used, because its Sunday is not posted at lock and its Saturday is about 96% posted. Its sd is the root-mean-square of (actual - mean4) over the 13 most recent target weeks W <= D-14 complete in the lock capture, each recomputed by the same rule from that one capture. Past weeks that fail the outage check are skipped, with a search depth of 26 weeks. If fewer than 13 weeks qualify, the round is not posted. This is Seattle's rev-3 spread rule, unchanged. The reference mean, sd and the four weekly counts are published and hashed with the question. The arena's generic date < lock filter would let the partial week in, so the adapter computes from whole weeks. Implementation (owner rule G1): add one parameterised reference to ssa/baselines.py, not a new name per card: zero_point {family: mean_k | yoy_k | persistence, k, spread: rms_n}. This card uses {family: mean_k, k: 4, spread: rms13}. Seattle's 'yoy4' is {family: yoy_k, k: 4, spread: rms13}, and persistence on D-14 is {family: mean_k, k: 1, spread: rms13}. A round without the key keeps today's 'persistence', so existing rounds do not move. Spread (owner rule G2): every reference shown or ranked carries its own measured rms13 spread over the window stated above, never the arena's default sd 1.5. Measured, all requests, modern backfill, as MAPE over 160 target weeks 2023-10-09 to 2026-10-26: mean4 6.65% (median 4.34%, max 42.0%); persistence on D-14 7.63%; Seattle-style yoy4 8.40%; yoy4 with last year's week smoothed over 3 weeks 7.96%. Mean CRPS with each reference's own 13-week RMS spread, over 146 weeks 2024-01-15 to 2026-10-26: mean4 3,813; persistence 4,196; yoy4 4,926. mean4 is the best in both of the last two years taken separately: +6.4% and +15.1% CRPS over persistence. yoy4 is the worst in both: -13.4% and -12.9%. Why yoy4 fails here and not in Seattle: NYC's large weeks are weather and one-off bursts. Examples are the week of 2026-01-26 at 111,196 (HPD heat 45,440 and DSNY snow 22,508 in one week), the week of 2026-02-23 (DSNY 26,068), and Noise-Residential bursts (29,873 in the week of 2024-12-30, against about 7,000 normally). yoy4 multiplies by a single week from last year and imports last year's shock into this year: +48% at New Year 2026, -53% in the week of 2026-01-26. Holiday weeks, error of mean4 / persistence / yoy4: Thanksgiving 2025 +10.8% / +11.2% / +0.6%; Christmas 2025 +34.4% / +46.8% / +21.9%; New Year 2026 +22.1% / +19.7% / +48.3%; July 4 2026 -10.3% / -12.8% / -4.0%. mean4 leaves holiday credit on the table, and the doc's principle that seasonal patterns should score about 0 is not met at Christmas by any of the three. Shown on the board, not ranked: persistence (mean_k k=1) and yoy_k k=4, each with its own rms13 spread.
resolution: The first fresh archived snapshot (X-SODA2-Data-Out-Of-Date false) at or after Tuesday 12:00 America/New_York, eight days after the target week ends, whose X-SODA2-Truth-Last-Modified is after Monday 18:00 ET, so that it carries Monday evening's load. Example: target 2026-12-14 to 2026-12-20, snapshot Tue 2026-12-29 12:00 ET. The value is that snapshot's sum for the seven target days. The archived body and headers are the record. Later revisions never change a resolved round. Fill-in, measured, not piloted: Socrata's system field :created_at (row insert time) shows when each row first appeared. Over the 41 target weeks 2026-01-05 to 2026-10-12, the share of each week's current count still missing at the last load before resolution (Monday W+14) had a median of 0.0026% and a max of 0.734% (week of 2026-03-16). Only 2 weeks were above 0.5%. Per request: 95.8% post within 1 day, 99.65% within 3 and 99.96% within 14; the longest lag was 224 days [verified computation, query of 2026-11-09T01:06Z]. Limits: :created_at was reset for all 3.46 million rows re-inserted on 2025-12-26 (the dataset split), so earlier weeks cannot be measured. Rows deleted after posting are invisible to this method. Two vintages (truth 11-05 and truth 11-08) showed no decrease on any of 65 days, and growth only in the last 10 [verified]. So the doc's 7-day lag is ample. Owner rule G3 waives the unscored pilot of two or more rounds, because this card measured late fill-in directly. One confirmation check is kept, on real captures: on Fri 2026-12-11 a maintainer compares the week of 2026-11-23 to 11-29 in the Tue 12-08 snapshot (+8) against the Fri 12-11 snapshot (+11). If growth is under 0.5%, the 2026-12-13 round is scored. If not, that round runs unscored, which is announced before its lock, and a new revision sets a longer lag. This needs daily captures running from Tue 2026-12-08.
missing_data_policy: (1) No fresh resolution snapshot by Friday 12:00 ET after the scheduled time: the round is cancelled, never resolved from a later pull. (2) Outage check on the resolution snapshot. A target day fails if its total is below 40% of the median daily total over the 28 days before the target week, or if any of NYPD, HPD, DSNY, DOT or DEP (together about 88% of requests) has zero rows that day. If a day fails, the next fresh daily snapshot inside the grace window is used. If the check still fails at the end of the window, the round is cancelled. Calibration: in 1,497 days from 2022-10-01 the lowest real day ratio was 0.57 (Christmas Day 2023 and 2025). None of those five agencies had a zero day in 797 days from 2024-09-01, with minimum daily counts of 2,164 / 473 / 231 / 151 / 185 [verified computation]. A per-agency 40% rule was rejected: real HPD days fall to 31% of their 4-week same-weekday median after cold spells. (3) Reference at lock: if any of the four reference weeks has a day failing the same check, the block steps back one week (weeks starting D-42, D-35, D-28 and D-21), and the question text says so. If it still fails, the round is not posted. (4) Posting gaps are normal: in 2026, eight days posted fewer than 1,000 rows (06-13, 07-16, 08-13, 09-10, 10-07, 10-11, 11-02, 11-03), and the next load caught up each time [verified]. Because the reference ends at D-8 and resolution is at +8 days, a gap affects a round only if it lasts more than about 5 days. (5) A stale-secondary body (Out-Of-Date true) is never archived as a capture. It is logged as a failed fetch. (6) A new agency code is counted, since the population is all requests, and logged. (7) If the dataset ID changes again, as it did when the data was split in December 2025, the family pauses and a new card revision follows. (8) Historical backtests use today's backfill, not first prints, and are labelled that way.
scoring: SSA topline scoring for a predictive distribution over the weekly count: mean and sd (sd > 0) or a quantile map including 0.5, scored with CRPS. Arena target_type continuous_normal. Skill is 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(zero point), with the zero point being the round's zero_point reference (mean_k k=4, rms13, owner decision rev 2), a normal with the baseline rule's mean and its 13-week RMS spread, published and hashed at lock. Check that submitting the reference scores about 0 (lesson 12), on 146 weeks: an entrant who submits mean4's mean and only rescales its sd gains at most +0.6% (k 0.85). mean4's 90% interval covers 83% of weeks, because the tails are heavy (weather weeks), and its sd ran 2,309 to 17,486. With the arena's fixed persistence sd of 1.5 as the zero point, the same entrant would gain +21.5%. Free skill if a weaker zero point is ranked: with yoy4 as the zero point, an entrant who simply submits mean4 with its honest spread scores +22.6%. With persistence on D-14, +9.1% [verified computation]. Movement check (arena scoring.noise_floor, last 52 weeks, all requests): noise m = 4,564, real movement s = 6,414, ceiling term m/sqrt(pi) = 2,575, so the series is scoreable. Level: weekly mean 60,014 in late 2022, 61,894 in 2023, 66,381 in 2024, 69,803 in 2025 and 77,033 in 2026 so far: a steady rise of about 6% a year. The last 8 weeks (2026-09-07 to 10-26) were 77,025 / 76,778 / 73,002 / 79,179 / 75,346 / 76,445 / 82,210 / 80,677. Over 52 weeks the min was 57,403 (Christmas 2025) and the max 111,196 (week of 2026-01-26). Also shown, not ranked: skill against persistence and yoy4, median absolute error, and 50%/90% interval coverage. Maintainers confirm whether the noise term applies to an administrative count (docs/sources.md §1.4).

Rev-2 decisions by Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08: zero point A, mean4 with an rms13 spread; population A, all requests; route A, automated once a person has read the NYC.gov Terms in a browser, with the manual weekly download as the documented fallback; first scored lock 2026-12-13, together with Seattle. [verified computation, 2026-11-09T01:05:03Z] 52 weeks (2025-11-03 to 2026-11-01), 3,965,541 requests. Top problems: NYPD Illegal Parking 15.6%; NYPD Noise - Residential 10.5%; HPD HEAT/HOT WATER 8.9%; NYPD Blocked Driveway 4.9%; NYPD Noise - Street/Sidewalk 4.4%; HPD UNSANITARY CONDITION 3.5%; DOT Street Condition 3.1%. [verified computation, modern backfill, daily counts 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-05 from two grouped queries at 01:04Z and 01:11Z] Reference comparison for all requests. evidence.finding: [owner input, checked] The doc proposes all requests, count(distinct unique_key), Mon-Sun NY weeks, lock Sunday 23:59 ET, resolution Tuesday 12:00 ET after a 7-day lag, and the previous week as baseline. This card keeps the population, window, lock and resolution. It changes the baseline: the previous week lacks its Sunday and about 4% of its Saturday at lock, so it is not available. Findings against the doc: the 60 s timeout in its sample code is shorter than a stale-secondary answer (59-68 s). Its freshness check on rowsUpdatedAt cannot detect a stale secondary, but the X-SODA2-Data-Out-Of-Date header can.
